claims.text: In the space of just three weeks, the UN Human Rights Office documented 15 drone strikes on El Obeid, which killed at least 45 civilians. El Obeid has more than half a million residents, together with at least 100,000 internally displaced persons, and the number of newly displaced people across Kordofan has risen by nearly two-thirds in only three months.

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA: renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan state, have put civilians, critical infrastructure and humanitarian operations at risk. UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher said humanitarians are scaling up efforts to reach families hit by conflict in North Kordofan and will seize every opening to expand lifesaving aid in and around El Obeid. OCHA noted that approximately $1.2 billion of the $2.9 billion required for Sudan's 2026 humanitarian response had been received. No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid was published in this update.

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA: 'Renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid ... have also put civilians, critical infrastructure and humanitarian operations at risk.' No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+).

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA, reports renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid threatening civilians, infrastructure and humanitarian operations, and cites more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city — a figure of different scope from WFP's 17 July count of 120,000+ in the Unified IDP Camp alone. No new aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (at least 45 civilians killed).

UN News (10 August 2026), citing OCHA: RSF forces have encircled El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, threatening a full-scale ground assault as civilians flock to the city and surrounding areas in search of safety and assistance. Humanitarian partners delivered two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe water shortages. The UN Secretary-General's Personal Envoy has held meetings with both sides and is working toward a full cessation of hostilities. No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid was published in this update, beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+).

UN News (12 August 2026), citing OCHA: 'Multiple waves of drone strikes were reported on Wednesday across El Obeid, the North Kordofan capital'... 'roughly 15,000 families have been displaced to El Obeid over the past three weeks,' driven by continuing attacks and insecurity in northern parts of the state, with OCHA noting the influx is 'putting greater pressure on displacement sites and basic services that are already overstretched.' This is a new inflow-displacement figure, distinct in scope from the existing cumulative death toll (45+ killed, UN Human Rights Office, 3 July 2026) and the Unified IDP Camp population figure (120,000+, WFP, 17 July 2026); no new aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid was reported.

Save the Children, via ReliefWeb (14 August 2026): "Nearly 39,000 children fled to the city of El Obeid in North Kordofan, Sudan, over the first six months of the year, escaping violence and attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure that have uprooted families across the state... The new arrivals are now part of more than 605,000 people living in El Obeid town and Sheikan locality... In April 2026, Save the Children-supported health facilities in Sheikan locality treated 426 children for malnutrition, compared with 195 in March, marking a 118% month-on-month increase... individual [water] consumption has now been reduced to approximately 7 litres per person per day, less than half of the general minimum standard of 15 litres recommended by the World Health Organization during crises."

G7 Foreign Ministers' joint statement on El Obeid, Sudan (14 July 2026): condemns ongoing RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and obstruction of humanitarian access, references the precedent of atrocities in El Fasher, and calls for an immediate ceasefire and compliance with the Jeddah Declaration to protect civilians.

UN News (10 August 2026): RSF drone attacks continue on El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, even as the UN and partners have provided two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe water shortages; separately, 18,000 people were displaced from over 20 villages in West Darfur in the preceding week, and 75,000 displaced persons were cut off from care after three health facilities closed in Central Darfur. Sudan-wide, more than 30 million people need assistance, over 9 million are internally displaced, and the US$3 billion humanitarian appeal is only about 40% funded (US$1.2 billion received).

UN News, 'Sudan war: 200,000 newly displaced as fighting and floods intensify' (19 August 2026): heavy fighting and drone strikes on El Obeid city's main electrical transformer have triggered prolonged power outages, disrupting water pumping, health facilities and telecommunications; more than 200,000 people have been newly displaced across the wider Kordofan region since late 2025, and displacement in Sheikan locality (which contains El Obeid) has surged by 25 percent in the past eight months.

NRC report (posted 7 July 2026) on El Obeid: families are dying from drone strikes and from hunger as the siege continues, with an aid convoy struck the preceding week; essential services and food access are collapsing further as the blockade persists.

UN News (17 July 2026): the UN human rights chief warned that civilians in El Obeid "have been under siege for 18 months" and face continuous drone strikes, with more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city. WFP is providing food assistance to over 100,000 people in those camps, including nutrition support for 17,000 children, but is distributing only a reduced ration that recipients are sharing with other families. Almost 20 million people in Sudan are now classified as acutely food insecure, and more than 14 million people have been uprooted nationwide since the conflict began.

WFP Geneva Palais briefing note (published 17 July 2026): El Obeid city (population approximately 500,000) is hosting displaced people, with more than 120,000 people in the 'Unified IDP Camp' alone. WFP is providing food/cash assistance to just over 100,000 people in camps inside the city, but severe funding shortfalls mean recipients are only receiving 50 percent of the ration they should. Fuel scarcity has crippled partner logistics, forcing WFP to deploy its own fleet vehicles to keep distributions running.

UNFPA Flash Update #2 on the situation in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan (published 20 July 2026, covering 1-19 July): 21 drone-related incidents were recorded in and around El Obeid between 1-19 July 2026, causing civilian casualties (no aggregate death toll given), damage to critical infrastructure, and further disruption to already-limited essential services, with severe constraints on sexual and reproductive health and gender-based-violence response services due to insecurity and resource shortages.

UN News (24 July 2026), citing a UN Women statement: 'More than half a million people live [in El Obeid], including 83,000 internally displaced people, most of them women and children.' Drone strikes have targeted water points and distribution sites during the day, forcing women and girls to wait until nightfall to collect water, where they face sexual violence instead — UN Women describes this as leaving 'no safe window' to access water. Nationwide, 'drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians in the first four months of 2026 alone — more than 80 per cent of all civilian deaths recorded by the human rights office in that period.' The number of women and girls needing gender-based-violence services nationwide has quadrupled since the conflict began, reaching an estimated 12.7 million in 2026, and cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July.

description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary fighters have besieged El Obeid, the capital of Sudan's North Kordofan state, subjecting the city to sustained drone strikes and blockade, and UN News reported on 10 August 2026 that RSF forces had encircled the city and were threatening a full-scale ground assault. The UN Human Rights Office documented 15 drone strikes in three weeks that killed at least 45 civilians (3 July), and WFP counted more than 120,000 displaced people in the city's Unified IDP Camp alone (17 July), with rations cut to 50 percent of the full entitlement by funding shortfalls. Displacement into the city continues: OCHA reported roughly 15,000 families arriving over three weeks in mid-August, and Save the Children says nearly 39,000 children fled to the city in the first six months of the year, with El Obeid town and Sheikan locality now hosting more than 605,000 people. No ceasefire has been confirmed and the siege remains ongoing.

impact.summary: The most recent aggregate figures for El Obeid remain at least 45 civilians killed (UN Human Rights Office, 3 July 2026) and more than 120,000 people sheltering in the Unified IDP Camp (WFP, 17 July), while OCHA reported roughly 15,000 families newly displaced into the city over the three weeks to 12 August. Humanitarian partners have delivered two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe shortages, and Sudan's wider response remains underfunded, with US$1.2 billion received of the US$3 billion required. RSF forces have encircled the city; no ceasefire or lifting of the siege has been confirmed.

event.scale: City under siege and now encircled by RSF forces; UN human-rights atrocity-risk warning; UN warns of threatened full-scale ground assault
